source: Union Budget 2024 capital-gains regime (effective 23 Jul 2024): listed-equity/equity-MF LTCG 12.5% with a ₹1,25,000/FY exemption (Section 112A, as amended by Finance (No. 2) Act 2024), STCG 20% (Section 111A). Crypto (Virtual Digital Assets) taxed flat 30% under Section 115BBH regardless of holding period, and Section 115BBH(2) expressly disallows setting off a VDA loss against any other income, including another VDA's gains.

notes: Not tax advice. No cess (4% Health & Education Cess) or surcharge is added on top of these rates. No indexation benefit is modeled (removed for most assets by the 2024 Budget, with a grandfathered pre-2001 exception not modeled here).

MUTUAL_FUND rows assume an equity-oriented scheme (>=65% equity allocation). Debt-oriented mutual fund units acquired on/after 1 Apr 2023 are, per the Finance Act 2023 amendment, taxed entirely at the investor's slab rate with NO long-term concessional rate regardless of holding period — this app does not currently distinguish equity vs. debt mutual funds (MutualFundHolding has no such flag), so debt-fund users will see an incorrect (too favorable) LTCG rate here. Flagged as a known limitation, not silently wrong.

CRYPTO: Section 115BBH also disallows deducting any expense (other than acquisition cost) and disallows loss set-off against ANY other income, including gains on a different crypto asset — lossOffsetAllowed: false on this row means the tax-loss-harvesting scan MUST exclude Indian crypto holdings from harvesting suggestions entirely, not just skip offsetting them.
1% TDS on crypto transfers (Section 194S) is not modeled — this is a withholding mechanism, not a final tax liability, and doesn't change the totals this report shows.
